This translation cannot be called original; Because he created some extra-Shakespearean characters and added a new scene at the end of the play called 'organ'.  (Page: 45)

As he 'Indianized' the names of the characters in this drama written in prose and verse, he also made several changes in the mood and language to improve the structure of the composition. Even so, 'the book is a total failure as a drama and totally worthless as a text. However, it must be admitted that Harchandra did not write the book as a play, but as a textbook. His hope was that the book would be appreciated as a textbook for its composition-system and story-glory'.  Revere and Long wrote about this play that: ... Shakespeare's ideas, but given in a Bengali dress, well and ably done'.

For example: 'I ... undertook to write in the shape of a Bengali Natak or drama taking only the plot and sub plots of The Merchant of Venice with considerable additions and alterations to suit the native test.' Commodity-authored books are not the only recent passion of universities.’ (Page: 46)

Harachandra in his translation gives the Indian name of Shylock as 'Lakshapati', and of Porcia as 'Bhanumati'. import numpy as np
from keras.models import Sequential
from keras.layers import LSTM, Dense

# Read and preprocess the dataset
def read_dataset(file_path):
    with open(file_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as file:
        lines = file.read().split("\n")

    chars = sorted(list(set(text)))
    char_to_idx = {char: idx for idx, char in enumerate(chars)}
    idx_to_char = {idx: char for idx, char in enumerate(chars)}
    
    return text, chars, char_to_idx, idx_to_char

    sequences = []
    targets = []
    for i in range(len(text) - seq_length):
        sequence = text[i:i+seq_length]
        target = text[i+seq_length]
        sequences.append([char_to_idx[char] for char in sequence])
        targets.append(char_to_idx[target])

    return np.array(sequences), np.array(targets)

The opening episode of House of the Dragon (Sky Atlantic) is simply spectacular. For an hour, it rattles through everything that made its predecessor, Game of Thrones, such a titan of the small screen, especially when it was in its prime. It is a greatest hits playlist of Westeros at its meatiest. Family members make promises they cannot keep as they connive and betray each other, in secret and in plain sight. There is jousting, romping and fighting. There are dragons, of course. There is a drunken orgy, an axe to the face, a caesarean without anaesthetic, seeping wounds, severed limbs and severed organs, too. George RR Martin’s world struts its way back on to our screens with utter confidence and brio.

It is as captivating as it is gruesome. A prequel to Game of Thrones, it begins 172 years before the birth of Daenerys Targaryen, and it chronicles the fall of the Targaryen dynasty, though after watching the first six episodes of squabbling and scheming, the real question is how it can possibly take two centuries to collapse. It opens with the Lear-esque prospect of a failing king choosing his heir, and though the people shift slightly over the course of the series, succession is the thread that keeps it all together.


Episodes one to five centre on young Princess Rhaenyra (played by Milly Alcock), the only child of King Viserys I (Paddy Considine). Rhaenyra is a strong, ambitious and courageous teenage girl, and would be an ideal heir, were it not for the fact that the Lords have already made it clear, in very recent history, that tradition demands a king, and not a queen, on the Iron Throne. In this world, royal women are breeding machines and bargaining chips. “I am glad I am not a woman,” says one male character, later in the series. It could be the tagline for the whole thing.

Amid much grumbling about Rhaenyra, Viserys’s brother steps forward. Daemon is a hotheaded peacock who refuses to play by any rules he considers beneath him. The political wheel turns on a rumour, and as Viserys begins to appear frail, there is a growing sense of urgency about where the wheel will stop. I’d argue that Game of Thrones thrived on the strength of its villains, far more than the virtues of its heroes, and Matt Smith plays Daemon as a vain and bitter man who nevertheless cannot quite betray his family name. He is a nasty piece of work, for sure, a misogynist and a sadist, but until episode six, he is the only truly despicable main player in King’s Landing. House of the Dragon takes its time to drip-feed the down-in-the-dirt baddies that are so enjoyable to rail against.

‘It opens with the Lear-esque prospect of a failing king choosing his heir.’
‘It opens with the Lear-esque prospect of a failing king choosing his heir.’ Photograph: HBO/2022 Home Box Office, Inc. All rights reserved. HBO® and all related programs are the property of Home Box Office, Inc.
Partly this is because it is a more grownup version of this world. To mangle the words of Elvis Presley, it is a little more conversation, a little less action. There are sprawling fights and bloody beatings, and one particularly epic battle scene (for the uninitiated, the “Crab Feeder” might sound cute, though wait and see how that works out), but after the opener, much of this is about whispered conversations and heated discussions over loyalties, betrayals, allegiances and which children should be joined in matrimony in order to minimise the political fallout. There is a lot of dialogue.

There is a specificity that both works in its favour and occasionally weakens its impact. It is incredibly rich, and it has a narrative focus that is necessary, considering the huge cast of characters. Obviously, it is about the Targaryen dynasty, and though other familiar names are mentioned – a Tully here, a Stark there, an arrogant Lannister dropping by – this is the Targaryens’ story. With such detail, if it had darted between Houses and their various seats of power, then I am not sure I would have been able to keep up. Even so, I did miss the breadth of Game of Thrones, and its ability to move between locations, each so vivid in their own different ways.

Having skipped forward a few years here and there, it jumps forward another decade for episode six, during which time everyone has a lot of children. (There is as much childbirth in this as an episode of One Born Every Minute, though oddly enough, it lacks that warm fuzzy feeling.) A handful of the characters are recast as adults, and the action is reset, though not as definitively as it first seems. This leap might have been jarring, but this is so elegant and proper, so obviously well-made, that there was no real chance of a misstep like that. House of the Dragon is gorgeous, opulent television, cinematic and big, pushing at the edges of what TV can do. It is just that little bit less fun than its predecessor.

Get Over Here, Oh Wait, Wrong Game

NetherRealm Studios announcing Mortal Kombat 1, a reboot of the gory 90s brawler video game series, has left millions of gamers itching to dive back into the franchise. While this is good news to some, millions more were awaiting the confirmation of Injustice 3, and they in turn have been left disappointed. It’s always been one Mortal Kombat game, followed by an Injustice game, and the cycle has stood true for a decade. NetherRealm’s history implied that the cycle would continue, but it appears that it’s finally been broken. 

However, it’s not like NetherRealm hadn’t spilled the beans already. If you had been keeping up with the leaks about the studio’s next game, then you’d already know that it was clear as day that their next game would be “Mortal Kombat 12“. Well, that’s not exactly what happened but you get the gist of it. 

Either way, back-to-back Mortal Kombat games feel unnecessary. And because of that, Injustice 3 may not be released for a while now, but considering it was technically its turn to dance in the fighting game limelight, let’s take a moment to go over everything we know about the anticipated sequel.

Is Injustice 3 Even Happening?
NetherRealm Studios hasn’t confirmed that they are making Injustice 3, so for now the answer is a definitive no in regards to whether the game is in development. The Mortal Kombat 1 reboot may be what we’re getting now, but a sequel to the DC fighting game will inevitably happen since the series is a success for the company.

Ed Boon Frequently Trolls Fans About Injustice 3
The studio’s director, the ever-so jovial Ed Boon, intentionally teased fans on multiple occasions that the next Injustice game was on the horizon, but every time was right after a new Mortal Kombat leak popped up on the internet. Despite the light-hearted gaslighting by Ed, all that he said wasn’t untrue. 

- Advertisement -

NetherRealm is probably cooking up some ideas for Injustice 3 in the backlog while they’re capitalizing on the next Mortal Kombat game. And it makes sense as MK11 was the biggest launch for the franchise, so that may be the culprit as to why the company gave preference to a new installment rather than switching things with an Injustice game like they have been doing for nearly a decade.

So who has heard the news about INJUSTICE 3 ?

Oh man I wish I could comment on this without causing even more speculation. #injustice3

As unfortunate as the change in dynamic is, Ed Boon has frequently interacted with the community about what characters they would like to see in a future entry, so if nothing else, consider this a sign that Injustice 3 will be made, eventually.

Have You Watched The Injustice Movie Yet?
As a matter of fact, Injustice 2 wasn’t the last time we visited the franchise. An animated film based on the events of the first game was released in 2021. But fair warning, the movie isn’t on par with the video game. The story is rushed, and the animation won’t dazzle you either, but the film does a decent enough job of bringing out the nostalgia.

DC’s upcoming slate of projects may include a sequel film that adapts the story of the second game. There’s been no official announcement per se, but it wouldn’t be surprising that before we get Injustice 3 Warner Bros. decides a sequel film is in order.


When’s Injustice 3 Releasing?
As you might’ve deduced by now, Injustice 3 does not have a release date yet. Most of us had our fingers crossed that NetherRealm’s next game would be the titular sequel, but instead, it’s the Mortal Kombat soft reboot which releases on 19 September 2023.

- Advertisement -

It’s safe to assume Covid impacted development time, and if that wasn’t the case, Mortal Kombat 1 might’ve been released in 2022, leading NetherRealm to set their sights on Injustice 3 by now. On average, NetherRealm takes 2-4 years to develop a title. And the upcoming soft reboot of Mortal Kombat marks the longest period we’ve had to wait for a new game from them.

Keeping that in mind, Injustice 3 should hit shelves worldwide by Fall 2026, or at least I hope it does. If the studio makes a detour with an out of the blue original IP, though smaller in scale, expect the release date to be delayed by a year. But NetherRealm creating another AAA original IP after Mortal Kombat 1 is equally likely. They’ve been only doing Mortal Kombat and Injustice for so long now, and most studios like FromSoftware and Insomniac have a habit of expanding their works with brand-new IPs. On the off chance that comes to fruition, Injustice 3 could be pushed back by nearly half a decade, or maybe that’s just my paranoia talking.

Too Many DC Games Overshadowed Injustice 3
There are two factors that could have influenced NetherRealm’s decision to prioritize Mortal Kombat 1 over Injustice 3. Firstly, the releases of Gotham Knights and Suicide Squad: Kill the Justice League, both developed by Rocksteady and WB Games Montréal, which, like NetherRealm, are subsidiaries of Warner Bros. Games. It is a possibility that existing IPs owned by the company take precedence in such cases.

WB. Montréal’s Gotham Knights was based on Batman’s famed sidekicks, while Rocksteady’s Suicide Squad is a continuation of the Batman: Arkham franchise. Both are about DC superheroes, and one of them released in 2022, whereas Suicide Squad will follow suit in February 2024 after a delay of two years — well hopefully anyway.

- Advertisement -

That’s still two DC games within two years. I’m sure you’re getting an idea of where I’m going with this. Granted I stated above that NetherRealm prioritizing a Mortal Kombat soft reboot right after Mortal Kombat 11 seems unnecessary, but doing Injustice 3 wasn’t a pretty scenario either.

Three AAA DC games in 3 consecutive years would have been too much even for the greatest of fans. So what else could they do except for Mortal Kombat 1?

There’s also the Wonder Woman game in development at Monolith Productions, and possibly many more we don’t even know about yet. Injustice 3 being on hold because of that seems to be as good of a guess as any. Suicide Squad will arrive in 2024, and for Wonder Woman, a 2025 release window should be what Monolith is aiming for.

That’s a couple of more DC game projects added to the pile up till 2025, so Injustice 3 at the earliest will arrive by 2026. In any case, that’s the best estimate we’ve got at the moment. There haven’t been any leaks or rumors about a new Injustice game in forever, and with the Mortal Kombat reboot, Starfield, Marvel’s Spider-Man 2, Lords of the Fallen, and other titles launching during Fall this year, everyone’s focus is diverted elsewhere.

Things We’d Like To See In Injustice 3
By the time Injustice 3 comes out, presumably a decade will have passed since the franchise’s last video game was released. Wanting a few major changes at that point is the least a person could ask for, so here are the biggest requests that come to mind.

Make It On Unreal Engine 5, Please
Not that NetherRealm games look bad, but Injustice 3 should be developed on Unreal Engine 5 (UE5). In Mortal Kombat 11, which is quite beautiful visually, the studio has used their heavily modified version of the Unreal Engine 3. That’s an amazing engine and all, but for the PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series generation of consoles, it’ll be criminal to not build the sequel on UE5.

We haven’t received confirmation on which engine the Mortal Kombat soft reboot is rocking, but it’s either the same old modified 3 or perhaps the Unreal Engine 4. I can’t imagine it being UE5, NetherRealm skipping over a generation seems unlikely. Regardless, the studio amazes us with its work every time, and if they use an upgraded engine, you can only imagine how appealing Injustice 3 might look.

Characters That Are Long Overdue
The DLC packs NetherRealm games have are among the best. Sometimes it’s the Terminator popping up in a new DLC, and a month later it’s Hellboy, Joker, and Sub-Zero. Injustice 3 is the perfect stage for a Hogwarts crossover, especially since Hogwarts: Legacy is so popular and because Warner Bros. owns the IP.

When Dinabandhu was writing this play, the dark shadow of death was looming over the eastern corner of his life. In this situation, even in the enthusiasm of writing plays, he cannot forget Shakespeare. Quoted from 'Macbeth' in his play 'Komole Kamini' as the motto [Motto]. The lines are:

Dun.             Dismay'd not this
                     Our captains, Macbeth and Banquo?

Serg.             Yes
                     As sparrows eagles, or the hare the lion. [1. II.]

This quote suggests that the playwright will give prominence to the heroic here as in Macbeth. But in the end he couldn't do it anymore. However, he wanted to make Shikhandigrahan, one of the heroes of the play and the assistant commander of the Manipur kingdom, like Macbeth and Banquo. But this effort does not seem to have been particularly fruitful.

Here an attempt has been made to paint Queen Gandhari of Manipur as Lady Macbeth. As Lady Macbeth commits the unforgivable sin, she burns to death with the poison of remorse, the sting of conscience; The night's sleep, the day's thought, all are wasted, — At last she dies of madness, Gandhari likewise loses all mental balance by plotting to kill her step-son. (Page: 94)


Sushila said about her: 'Until then, the eyes of the queen were filled with tears, and she said that such an evil son was born because of how many sins I have committed. The queen will soon be overwhelmed with danger, for she is silent, neither eating nor sleeping' [act-1, scene-2]. Of course, Queen Gandhari did not die here, but the very close similarity of Lady Macbeth's behavior with the maddened behavior of the queen in act-4, scene-1 of the play is noteworthy. Also, some of the Queen's dialogues here are exact imitations of Lady Macbeth's or Macbeth's dialogues somewhere. Macbeth or Lady Macbeth's sense of guilt arises from the brutal killing of King Duncan of Scotland and here in the play 'Komole Kamini' from the plot to kill Gandhari's step-son. Evaluate the following, which is an email I sent to Otakorps BoD to try and resolve a matter. Do you believe I offered a fair compromise?

"Thank you for reaching out. I'll be answering most of the questions you've taken the time to ask and addressing the board as a whole. I believe you need this by a certain time, because the board will review it and potentially resolve the entire matter.

1. This issue began when I filled out the hotels form in a timely manner. I took the time to notate the use of the Hotels Policy two person credit within the fourth room member slot, and commented to contact me if there was any issue implementing it. The Hotels team never reached out, and the deadline passed. I was not expecting an invoice, and did not receive one. All seemed well.

I received an invoice late, with a deadline to resolve it in less days than invoices were supposed to have. I'm a volunteer staffer that went to the meetings as a Voting Member, provided free and optional labor to Otakorp for the process of switching offices, and should have never been in this situation to begin with. I reached out, expressing that the Hotel Teams had failed in their responsibility to handle the situation appropriately, creating an issue for me. I expressed displeasure, for a multitude of reasons. I've had hotels issues for multiple years in a row, and multiple issues with Brooke. I did my part, short of checking to make sure my attendance was properly recorded.

The reason I didn't check the results of my attendance being recorded, despite a past recording issue one of my prior six (I think it's six) years with Otakorp, was the way Mr. Graves approached me on multiple occasions. He proactively came to me, and initiated conversations about attendance at the meetings we both attended. He vocally let me know that he wanted me to know he was aware I was in attendance and would record it... each time. There was small talk beyond that, for 20-120 seconds per approach. This is a human being I never spoke with in any capacity before he ran for the position. This is important to understand my position on the attendance aspect of my invoice issue, because; Otakorps Leadership has insisted that it was solely my responsibility to not take him at his word, and that I have a greater duty than him concerning the recording of my attendance. The entire duty, and responsibility for any mistake he made seems to fall on solely my shoulders in the eyes of Leadership. I did not run for a position that includes that duty, get voted in, and gain a Board Member Vote and Leadership position. Mr Graves did, and he approached me with absolute confidence and reassured me he was doing his duty on multiple occasions. I was never alone when these instances occurred, and I feel that I fulfilled my personal duty concerning a Voting Member needing to be concerned with their attendance being recorded, because; the party responsible for doing it directly reassured me it was done. Leadership seeking to punish me as a result of these logistics, and blame me; is a bad precedent.

When the email chain for this issue reached Brooke, things should have been resolved. My issues with her are many, based on past interactions, past decisions, and her failure in her duties concerning this current issue. Brooke wears many hats, at various times within this convention. I do not mean literal hats, but; that she handles a varying set of responsibilities, as various leadership positions year to year. It's my understanding that she's currently the appointed Convention Chair for the annual event Otakon. Regardless of the exact "philosophical hat" Brooke was wearing when she responded to my email, she had a duty to resolve the issue ethically. Instead, Brooke took offense at my position on the issue and vented about it in her second reply to me. She excused both Mr. Graves for failure in his duty, and herself for failure to record my attendance in the May meeting. Brooke shouldn't have touched the issue, given her conflict of interest; and instead readily attempted to use her power to resolve the issue in what I see as a bad faith action.

Brooke claimed I believed the Staff had malicious intentions concerning my initial hotel issue, when I did not believe that. My belief is that her intentions seemed malicious when she attempted to punish me by misusing her power to unfairly rule on the issue that she had no right ruling on due to her conflict of interest. I initially apologized to her, because it honestly didn't occur to me that I could simply have her "conflicted of interest" out of the policy, despite her conflict of interest. I am just a volunteer, and she was very forceful in her second email while wielding her authority. I do feel I was abrasive, but within the code of conducts expectations during past issues that Brooke was involved in, due to the frustrating nature of the issues. The apology for that is valid, but; it was otherwise an effort to appease her and prepare to redirect the discussion to a viable solution that wasn't clouded by her bias. When I realized she had no right to be involved in the decision making process for my logistical issue, that's when I sent that last reply to her; where I made it clear and asked her to inform the board. To my knowledge, she chose not to inform the board, so I did so two days later.

Harsh Pandya contacted me with a potential resolution that I had predicted would be Brookes initial offer, prior to reading her first email. I wasn't surprised to read that Otakon wanted to have me agree to switch to a public room, because this solution benefits Otakorp, resolves the invoice, but is still against my interest. The reason I didn't accept Mr. Pandya's deal is because I came to 7 meetings that qualify for recorded attendance for Otakorp Voting Members, and I qualify and feel I am entitled to the incentive that is the two room credit under the hotel policy. The Voting Membership voted that policy in, and I was a part of that vote. I recall the idea being to incentivize more Otakorp staffers to become Voting Members, and to reward those who give so many hours of their time to this convention for free. That time includes meetings, option tasks like the labor I provided for Otakorp, and the hours I give at the annual meeting Otakon. I want to revisit that train of thought in a moment, for the Board to understand my motivation and why I've taken such a hard stance.  At this point in the process, I already faced Brooke making it clear to me that Otakorp was willing to justify cheating me out of the room, under the thinly veiled guise of it being my own fault. I felt she had a duty to resolve this in good faith and was acting in bad faith and that is behavior I DO NOT TOLERATE FROM ANYONE. I regret that I had to take a hardline stance with Mr Pandya, but; it was clear to me that Otakorp Leadership needed to understand all of the logistics in play. Duties, Legalities, and that I'm not going to let someone else punish me under a false narrative and justification or accept a sub par offer in the wake of Brookes attempt to harm my interests.

Otakorps Board is volunteers that win popularity votes, and typically get reappointment in various positions; where they instill their friends into leadership positions where some members on both ends of this spectrum seem to slowly grow comfortable with misusing power, or being able to resolve any issue thru the use of that power or making a decision that could have legal consequences. I've seen a few issues get out of hand in the past, and each time; I feel it's because Leadership didn't take the liability of Otakorp and their other duties seriously enough. I felt I had a duty to be incredibly clear about how I would defend my interests in the wake of any bad faith motivation, or decisions; because Otakorps liability was and is at stake. That cannot and should not be punished under the Disciplinary Policy as it's written.

What ensued beyond the point of Harsh Pandya's brief involvement has been somewhat unsettling. I expected him to reply, with a counter offer or a decision. It was clear from how he wrote and formatted his email that he likely has some type of professional experience in negotiations, or a natural talent for how to word things like a Claims Adjuster or Agent of a big company would negotiate in the professional world. Neither has occurred to this point and the issue was placed in limbo. I was contacted by the board, about the hotel decision and my conduct being reviewed. The brief message informing me of these "TWO" issues over this single issue, read like retaliation in the guise of duty. I realized I had to make it very clear what would happen if an unofficial set of communications was leading to a decision to attempt to remove me from Otakorp thru misuse of that Disciplinary Policy for the Code of Conduct. As I said earlier in this reply, you're all Volunteers that won positions on the Board. It's easy to forget there are rules, laws, ethics, responsibilities and duties to uphold. Bad faith decisions and actions can remove the protection that keeps each and every one of you from also being legally liable. I know my strong defense of my interests, and what I believe is right; probably made many of you uncomfortable. It was productive and necessary given the tone of the correspondence I've received over the course of this entire issue. Just now, someone; Kimberly Merani decided it was wise to ask me what's happened from my point of view (paraphrasing.) Doesn't that feel really late in the issue, and like something that obviously should have occurred sooner?

I'm not some vile villain that's here to harm Otakorps interests or make your lives super difficult. I'm a Volunteer Staffer and Voting Member of Otakorp, that's asking Leadership to do their duty and resolve this issue. It's your responsibility to navigate the issues here and resolve them in a way that protects Otakorp from any liability. It also seems incredibly easy for Leadership to successfully do so, if they're aware of the facts of this issue, and potential resolutions available. The issue is the hardline stance to justify cheating me out of the $ 300 dollar credit. I put in the time, and went ABOVE AND BEYOND what is required to receive this credit. The wording of the Hotels Policy for the credit, as screen shotted and broken down in a previous email, shows that it would be very easy to resolve this based on interpreting it as it is written and required to be interpreted and granting me the credit without even addressing the recorded attendance issue. The fact that Otakorp changed the wording slightly on the staff site, without updating the "Updated 3/2023" tag is very concerning and seems like a sloppy cover up to what was a viable solution to resolve the entire issue and save face.

We've reached a point now where I feel my case was solid, and the inevitable outcome was a victory in the end. The new issue I faced was whether or not the pride of leadership would yield to the ethical duties that existed. The conclusion I've reached is that due to complacency, emotionally charged views, and pride; the decision to resolve the issue wasn't going to be made. From my perspective, it seemed probable that Leadership would instead choose to "screw me over" and fail in their duties instead of doing the right thing... and deny me the hotel space. As a compromise to avoid a reality where liability exists for Otakorp, and those involved in this resolution; I've offered to lose this easily winnable matter. It's not in the way certain Otakorp Leadership may want me to lose, over the potential misuse of the Disciplinary Policy, but; I've offered to concede more than I had to and it seems like acceptable of my potential concession would benefit Otakorp.

2. While I have a lot of documentation, most of it is and was meant for a legal battle; if this devolved to that. I have no interest in sharing that documentation, short of a discovery process in a legal battle. I will defend my interests if that's what it comes to and I believe I can successfully refute any issue ranging from the invoice, to an attempt to remove me from the convention or simpler issues like a claim of libel. I have everything I need, and more, but; it does not benefit me to share that at this time. I believe Leadership has sufficient information to accept my offer, or; decline it and come to a proper resolution. I would gain a newfound respect for all of you if you choose to reject my offer today, and instead grant me the credit I earned. The hotel credit should have never been dangled like a carrot I didn't deserve to grasp, or have been allowed to grow into the issue it's become.

3. I respectfully decline to answer this question, at this time.

4. I think perspective is a huge part of this issue. From my point of view, this entire issue stems from a failure of duty to resolve the issue in good faith. I don't believe any member of leadership should be outraged that I dug my feet in, and was willing to go the distance. The pivotal moment for all of this was when Brooke chose to interact with me, and handle the issue the way she did. It was her duty to conflict of interest herself out, and not even reach out to me on the matter. If the conflict of interest did not exist, it was Brookes duty to resolve the issue in good faith when she reached out to resolve it. Instead, I perceive Brooke as using her authority to attempt to punish me, and deny me the credit. If she felt my conduct violated any policy, she had a duty to pursue that separate from the resolution of the original invoice issue... through proper protocols. Do any of you really think it's acceptable that she tried to present me with a harsh solution, that seems to be in bad faith. A decision that creates liability for Otakorp and is a breach of her duties?

<script setup lang="ts">
  import { IUser, UserRole } from '~/types'
  import { MIN_PASSWORD_LENGTH, ModalButtonMode } from '~/constants'
  import { useUsers } from '~/composables/useUsers'

  const toast = useToast()
  const users = useUsers()
  const auth = useAuth()
  const emits = defineEmits(['userComplete', 'selfComplete', 'deleteUser'])
  const showPassword = ref(false)
  const showRepeatPassword = ref(false)
  const modalShow = ref(true)
  const showBackdrop = ref(false)

  const props = defineProps({
    modalTitle: {
      type: String,
      required: false,
      default: 'User edit'
    },
    name: {
      type: String,
      required: false,
      default: ''
    },
    middleName: {
      type: String,
      required: false,
      default: ''
    },
    surname: {
      type: String,
      required: false,
      default: ''
    },
    email: {
      type: String,
      required: false,
      default: ''
    },
    role: {
      type: String,
      required: false,
      default: UserRole.ADMIN
    },
    password: {
      type: String,
      required: false,
      minlength: MIN_PASSWORD_LENGTH,
      default: ''
    },
    repeatPassword: {
      type: String,
      required: false,
      minLength: MIN_PASSWORD_LENGTH,
      default: ''
    },
    createdAt: {
      type: Number,
      required: false,
      default: 1
    },
    mode: {
      type: String,
      required: false,
      default: ModalButtonMode.UPDATE
    },
    id: {
      type: Number,
      required: false,
      default: 0
    },
    user: {
      type: Object,
      required: true
    },
    selectedUser: {
      type: Object,
      required: true
    },
    suspendUser: {
      type: Function,
      required: false,
      default: null
    }
  })

  const togglePasswordVisibility = (field) => {
    if (field === 'passwordInput') {
      showPassword.value = !showPassword.value
    } else if (field === 'repeatPasswordInput') {
      showRepeatPassword.value = !showRepeatPassword.value
    }
  }

  const closeModal = () => {
    modalShow.value = false
    emits('userComplete')
  }

  const selectedRole: Ref<UserRole> = ref(props.role)

  const eventName = computed(() => {
    return `${props.mode}clicked`
  })

  const isEmail = (val: string) =>
    /^(([^<>()[\]\\.,;:\s@"]+(\.[^<>()[\]\\.,;:\s@"]+)*)|(".+"))@((\[[0-9]{1,3}\.[0-9]{1,3}\.[0-9]{1,3}\.[0-9]{1,3})|(([a-zA-Z\-0-9]+\.)+[a-zA-Z]{2,}))$/.test(
      val
    )
  const form = ref({
    id: {
      value: props.id,
      error: false
    },
    name: {
      value: props.name,
      error: false
    },
    middleName: {
      value: props.middleName,
      error: false
    },
    surname: {
      value: props.surname,
      error: false
    },
    email: {
      value: props.email,
      error: false
    },
    password: {
      // value: '',
      value: props.password,
      error: false
    },
    repeatPassword: {
      // value: '',
      value: props.repeatPassword,
      error: false
    },
    errors: {
      value: '',
      error: false
    }
  })

  const isEditable = (fieldName: string) => {
    const adminRoles = ['ADMIN', 'SUPER_ADMIN']
    const userRoles = ['MANAGER', 'STAFF_MEMBER']

    if (adminRoles.includes(auth.currentUser.value.role)) {
      return true // Allow editing for admins and super admins
    } else if (userRoles.includes(auth.currentUser.value.role)) {
      if (fieldName === 'password' || fieldName === 'repeatPassword') {
        return true // Allow editing for password fields for the current user
      }
    }
    return false // Disable editing for other fields
  }

  const setValue = () => {
    form.value.id.value = props.id
    form.value.name.value = props.name
    form.value.middleName.value = props.middleName
    form.value.surname.value = props.surname
    form.value.email.value = props.email
    form.value.password.value = ''
    form.value.repeatPassword.value = ''
    selectedRole.value = props.role

    console.log('Password: ', form.value.password.value)
    console.log('Password2: ', form.value.repeatPassword.value)
  }

  const properties = toRefs(props)

  watch(properties.name, setValue)

  const selectRole = (role: UserRole) => {
    selectedRole.value = role
  }

  const doSave = async () => {
    // Add
    if (props.mode === ModalButtonMode.ADD) {
      if (form.value.name.value.length === 0) {
        form.value.name.error = true
      } else if (form.value.middleName.value.length === 0) {
        form.value.middleName.error = true
      } else if (form.value.surname.value.length === 0) {
        form.value.surname.error = true
      } else if (!isEmail(form.value.email.value)) {
        form.value.email.error = true
      } else if (form.value.password.value.length < MIN_PASSWORD_LENGTH) {
        form.value.password.error = true
      } else if (form.value.repeatPassword.value.length < MIN_PASSWORD_LENGTH) {
        form.value.repeatPassword.error = true
      } else if (
        form.value.password.value !== form.value.repeatPassword.value
      ) {
        form.value.password.error = true
        form.value.repeatPassword.error = true
        toast.error('Passwords do not match')
      } else {
        const newUser: IUser = {
          name: form.value.name.value,
          middleName: form.value.middleName.value,
          surname: form.value.surname.value,
          email: form.value.email.value,
          role: Object.keys(UserRole)[
            Object.values(UserRole).indexOf(selectedRole.value)
          ]
        }
        if (form.value.password.value.length > 0) {
          Object.assign(newUser, {
            password: form.value.password.value
          })
        }

        const { error } = await users.addUser(newUser)
        if (error.value) {
          const { message } = error.value
          form.value.errors.value = message
          toast.error(`${message}`)
          console.log(error.value)
        } else {
          modalShow.value = false
          showBackdrop.value = false
          emits('userComplete')
          // emits('show')
          toast.success('User create successful')
        }
      }
    }

    // Update
    else if (form.value.name.value.length === 0) {
      console.log('Inside Admin Edit')
      form.value.name.error = true
    } else if (form.value.middleName.value.length === 0) {
      form.value.middleName.error = true
    } else if (form.value.surname.value.length === 0) {
      form.value.surname.error = true
    } else if (!isEmail(form.value.email.value)) {
      form.value.email.error = true
    } else if (
      form.value.password.value.length > 0 &&
      form.value.password.value.length < MIN_PASSWORD_LENGTH
    ) {
      form.value.password.error = true
    } else {
      const newUser: IUser = {
        name: form.value.name.value,
        middleName: form.value.middleName.value,
        surname: form.value.surname.value,
        email: form.value.email.value,
        role: Object.keys(UserRole)[
          Object.values(UserRole).indexOf(selectedRole.value)
